questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Interviews real-world scaling: fairness in multi-tenant KCNA ingestion under bursty traffic, preventing starvation and ensuring predictable latency for all tenants.

## Key Concepts
- Per-tenant quotas and bounded bursts
- Gateways and global scheduling
- Backpressure signaling and observability
- Canary-style validation

## Code Example
```javascript
class TokenBucket {
  constructor(rate, burst) { this.rate = rate; this.burst = burst; this.tokens = burst; this.last = Date.now(); }
  allow(n=1){ this._drip(); if(this.tokens>=n){ this.tokens-=n; return true; } return false; }
  _drip(){ const now=Date.now(); const elapsed=(now-this.last)/1000; this.tokens = Math.min(this.burst, this.tokens + elapsed*this.rate); this.last=now; }
}
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you monitor fairness and detect starvation?
- How would quotas adapt during traffic spikes?

## Why This Is Asked
Real-world KCNA deployments must protect data across tenants; this question probes envelope encryption design, key lifecycle, and how to audit and delete data without breaking consistency.

## Key Concepts
- Envelope encryption
- Per-tenant KEK/DEK lifecycle
- Key rotation with zero-downtime re-encryption
- Auditability and tenant-scoped deletion

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudocode for decrypting payload using tenant DEK
const wrappedDek = metadata.getTenantWrappedDek(tenantId);
const dek = kms.unwrapDek(tenantId, wrappedDek);
const plaintext = crypto.decrypt(payload, dek);
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you test key rotation without service disruption?
- How do you enforce least-privilege access per tenant across decryptors?
